I just pushed a new feature which I have been working on today in an effort to decrease the load on the server and at the same time try to create a better user experience. Nobody likes to wait for content to load and regardless of how powerful servers are, loading large amount of data is not possible without user noticing delays. This update specifically targets comment loading system and instead of grabbing every root comment with its children, the system now grabs only 10 root threads with their children. For longer threads, this seems more natural, but for threads with no or little children comments, this may feel a bit odd. When scrolling down to the bottom of the page, 10 more threads will automagically load and be appended to the bottom of the page but users can also click the load more button.

It is 1:26 AM here and I have to get up and go to school at 7:30 which is why I didn't get a chance to test this as much as I would want. So, as always, please feel free to test it out and comment here if you find discover anything weird.

Thank you and zZzzzz

Basically, my idea is to have true democracy in subverses and to make moderator actions visible to the users and for the users to be able to comment on them. I'll flesh out this idea a bit.

First I'll talk about the visibility of mod actions. My idea is that each subverse would have sub-subverse or metaverse or whatever where a bot would post automatic thread when a moderator of that subverse makes some mod action like removing a thread, renaming a thread, adding a flair to thread, banning a user, changing the sidebar or so on. Users would also be able to comment on these threads, giving them ability to voice their opinion on moderator behaviour without having to use the mainsubverse for such discussion and forcing the mods to listen to them. Of course, this would be something that is default for all subverses and couldnt be turned off, as with ability to turn off it would just remove any good this would or could do, giving the mods just hide from any critique from the community and removing their need to defend their actions.

Related to this something which would enforce the above. A button which would force new moderators to be instituted on subverse if the users, or subscribers, of that subverse feel like the mods have started to run amoc and the subverse has lost its direction. This would make the subverses more democratic as the users would have a say on almost every aspect of how it is run and able to remove moderation team if they dont agree how its run.

Of course both ideas need to be fleshed out more and they arent perfect. For example, it would probably be really easy to abuse that coup de at system and there should be someway to avoid it. I hope that this fosters at least some discussion and the voat administrator team takes at least some note of this. I believe this is the kind of thing that could and would really differentiate voat as the democratic, uncensored, freedom of speech community it wants to be.
Enforced visibility for mod actions/ability for the community to do a coup de at if they feel that the mod team has run out of control.
What are some good items for him? I was recommended Rod of Ages and Frozen Heart, but that's as much as I know. How can I enhance his natural abilities, and if possible, increase his damage?

Hey there! Cho'Gath can be built quite a few ways, and if you're going for damage I would recommend for sure to get RoA first. After that you have a few options:

If your team already has a tank go ahead and get a Void Staff, Rabadon's Death Cap, and if you feel like getting even more health a Rylai's Crystal Scepter.

If your team doesn't have a tank go ahead and grab a Seeker's Armgaurd followed by a Giant's Belt and then finish Zhonya when possible. Then build an Abyssal Scepter for magic resistance. If you still need more damage build your Giant's Belt into a Rylai's Crystal Scepter. If you need more tank build the Belt into a Randuin's Omen.

BOTH of these builds you should get a RoA. Against more AD or a fed ADC get Frozen Heart. Against more AP or a fed AP champ get a Banshee's Veil or Spirit Visage (i recommend Banshee's because Cho'Gath doesn't have very much health regen to benefit from Spirit Visage passive). Your boots you can get at any time and I recommend getting Mercury Treads and then Homegaurd's for enchant.

Remember it is all about knowing when to buy the items. You'll get great at deciding what to do when after a lot of experience :)

Thanks so much, this is exactly the kind of help I was looking for when I posted this. I just got Cho'Gath just a few days ago, and I've been playing RoA and Frozen Heart (then B.F. Sword if I get a chance). I can't wait to try out the rest of these items. They all seem really neat.
We all have those unforgettable sessions that either go crazy good or crazy bad, tell us about yours!

I've been playing D&D for 10 years now. And one of my favorite stories happened just last year during the D&D Next playtest. We were playing Dead in Thay which is a great dungeon crawl that takes place in the Doomvault. My party was rather large with 6 players (2 mages, a rogue, a monk, a ranger, and myself as a war cleric) , and all level 8. We had made our way through the Caverns of Chaos section and came upon the Eldritch Alter. We could tell that the alter had some bad voodoo, and the rest of the party wasn't too keen on messing with it. But the dammed mages had other plans...

One of the mages had picked up a random long sword, and didn't have much of a need for it. So he decided to set it on the alter. When he did, my war cleric dropped into a coma. My cleric wakes up and can sense his surroundings, but can't feel, see, or speak. The rest of my party is concerned since the cleric just dropped dead. The bard checked me out and found I was still alive. The mage then picked up the sword, and to both of our surprise, I could communicate with the mage. The mages put their collective heads of knuckle together and figured out that my consciousness has been taken out of my body and placed into the longsword. Well, hell.

They place the sword into my hands and I'm able to wake up. But if I drop the sword, and am out of contact with it for 1 hour, I'll die. So I smack them around and we move on. We make it to the Gate Cavern in the Forest of Recovery and we encounter a wight and a helmed horror. We dispatch the wight easy enough (well, the ranger would say otherwise since he took some serious life drain), and that just left the helmed horror. The helmed horror, if you're not familiar, has an AC 20, HP 60, immunities to force damage from magic missile spells, necrotic, poison, blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, intoxicated, paralyzed, stunned, unconscious, dehydration, disease, effects that require the target to see, petrification, poison effects, polymorph; doesn’t breathe, drink, eat, or sleep. And has resistances to cold, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical weapons that aren’t adamantine. This sonuvabitch was tough. But the mages had an idea. They wanted to override the helmed horror's programming. Our DM was all about "the rule of cool". If you have a good idea, he'll work with you to try to make it happen. So he said "ok, here's how we'll do this: on your (the mage's) turn, you can expend a your highest level spell slot as a Arcana Check. If you are able to make 6 successful checks in a row of increasingly difficult DCs, then you may be able to command the helmed horror.

So we set about keeping this monster busy for 3 rounds while the mages worked. I have no idea how they managed to roll so well. Both mages had an INT of 20, which gives their Arcana mods a total of +8. The first check of 1st round was DC 15, the first mage passes his check, the second DC in the 1st round was 17, the second mage crits. 2nd round saw a DC 19, the first mage crits. The second DC for the 2nd round was 21, the second mage rolls a 19. Holy shit, they've almost done it. The 3rd round brought the DC to 23 (the DM at this point said he didn't think they'd get this far and was beginning to wish he hadn't agreed to this), the first mage needs to roll a 15 to meet the DC. He rolls a 17. We're all on the edge of our seat. The last check comes, DC 27. The second mage needs a 19 or 20. Anything less, and they will just have spent all their 4th level spells and one of their 3rd level spells for nothing. The mage takes his d20, shakes it in his hand, and lets it roll. 19. Nine-motherfucking-teen. We couldn't believe it. We all jumped up and and cheered. The Dm hung his head. He had handed over a nearly unstoppable construct to his players. But we weren't done yet.

We talked about what we should do with it, and the monk said "tarrasque, you should hand it your sword." That was a brilliant idea. I had my sword to the helmed horror, my cleric body falls to the ground. I have to make a DC 20 WIS saving throw to prevent to the helmed horror from rejecting me taking over his body. I nailed it. I had taken over the body of a helmed horror. I was immune to nearly everything. I could fly and cause death and destruction everywhere I went. I could not be stopped. It was beautiful. One of my absolute favorite campaigns I've ever played.

TLDR: I am Iron Man!

Holy crap man. Just holy crap. Kudos to your DM for sticking with what he said. Has he made the campaign more difficult since you're now so unstoppable? How does it go with you talking to NPCs and the like?
